content:
leah: Quick heads up, running into steady memory creep on long streaming sessions with heavy tool loops. Repro run: 6h, slope becomes noticeable after ~8-12m.
leah: Quick heap table from pprof (MB):
```
00:00  86.7
00:10  110.9  <-- growth onset
01:00  290.4
06:00 1284.7
```
leah: Metrics: kv.pages_total rises constantly, kv.reclaim_count flat, kv.page_evictions ~very low.
leah: Host: hosted-prod-us-west, runtime build d9f8e7 (opt-v2), kernel=auto, batch_window_ms=5, batching=continuous.
niko: Is this strictly tool-loop sessions or also plain streaming chat? any diff with tool calls disabled?
sam: If evictions are low while pages increase, likely references aren't being dropped (fragmentation or phantom pins).
leah: Disabling tool calls reduces growth a lot (only ~+120MB over 6h). Tool loops amplify.
devon: Two immediate probes: 1) force reclamation: KV_MAX_RESIDENCY_MS=300000 on a canary; 2) page coalesce trace: `./tools/trace_pages --session <id> --duration 10m --coalesce` + `pprof --proto /tmp/pprof.pb`.
maria: Note: PR #1428 kv-pool refactor changed pin/unpin ordering. I recall a potential dangling ref case when sessions rebind tools. Worth validating by rolling back.
leah: Rolling back PR #1428 locally reduced growth ~4x. Forced eviction dropped growth ~3x on canary but didn't eliminate it.
niko: Also try kernel override: kernel=latency-prioritized vs default-opt-v2. We saw different allocation shapes before.
sam: If rollback helps, let's bisect PR range. If not, add a repro harness that simulates frequent tool rebind + small binary attachments to stress pin paths.
leah: Current repro command:
```
./bin/repro --mode longstream --session-count 1 --duration 6h --tool-loop --attach-freq 30s --metrics kv.pages_total,kv.page_evictions,kv.reclaim_count
```
infra-bot: cgroup mem for pool redwood-prod-gpu-07 jumped 48% -> 87% during run. Logs /var/logs/infra/mem-spike-4412.log. No OOM kill.
devon: Capture allocator hist: `RT_ALLOC_HIST=1 ./bin/repro ...` -> saves alloc.hist. Also enable heavy tracing: `KV_REFTRACE=1` to get refcount stacks.
leah: Scheduled canary at 02:00 UTC to not impact primary traffic. Will attach flamegraphs + KV_REFTRACE output.
maria: Once you have KV_REFTRACE, I can parse refcount paths and look for unbalanced pin/unpin sites.
repro-bot: repro queued (job_id=R-4412-02). Artifacts at /tmp/repro/R-4412-02/.
leah: First KV_REFTRACE sample shows repeated +1 increments from `tool_bind()` without corresponding -1 on tool_unbind() when attachment path triggers fast-path exit. Stack excerpt: `runtime::kv_pin -> tool_bind -> attach_handler -> tool_loop`.
sam: That matches the refactor risk. Could be missing scoped unpin in early-return. Add ASAN-style check in unpin code to assert refcount not leaked.
devon: Also gather slab occupancy hist and page fragmentation: `kv.page_slab_hist` + `kv.page_chunk_free_pct`.
leah: After adding an extra unpin in the early-return path, local repro shows near-zero steady growth for 6h. Need more confidence in e2e.
maria: Good. Proposed plan: 1) revert PR #1428 in a hotfix on canary, 2) add unit test covering tool rebind+early exit, 3) add a longsession reclamation e2e test that runs weekly.
niko: During canary, toggle kernel=latency-prioritized to check allocation/fragmentation differences. If kernel affects not just perf but memory layout, we should track kernel+refactor interaction.
leah: Action items: collect full pprof + KV_REFTRACE on canary, run alloc.hist, run with forced eviction env, and test kernel override. I'll post artifacts here.
sam: Also add a metric alert: if kv.pages_total grows >50% over 1h without matching evictions, page a pager.
leah: Thanks everyone, posting traces in ~8h. :thumbsup:
